title: Valid Number
summary: Given a string s, determine if it represents a valid number according to the following rules: - An integer number can be defined with an optional sign ('+' or '-') followed by one or more digits.
statement: Given a string s, determine if it represents a valid number according to the following rules: - An integer number can be defined with an optional sign ('+' or '-') followed by one or more digits. - A decimal number can be defined with an optional sign ('+' or '-') followed by: - Digits followed by a dot ('.'). - Digits followed by a dot ('.') followed by digits. - A dot ('.') followed by digits. - An integer or decimal number can optionally be followed by an exponent notation ('e' or 'E') followed by an integer number. Examples of valid numbers include: "2", "0089", "-0.1", "+3.14", "4.", "-.9", "2e10", "-90E3", "3e+7", "+6e-1", "53.5e93", "-123.456e789". Examples of invalid numbers include: "abc", "1a", "1e", "e3", "99e2.5", "--6", "-+3", "95a54e53".
constraints: 1–20 characters, each an English letter, decimal digit, '+', '-', or '.'. Whitespace is not part of the input domain.
A mantissa is an optionally signed integer or decimal with at least one digit; a decimal may omit digits on one side of its dot, but not both.
An optional e/E exponent must be an optionally signed integer with at least one digit and no dot. Special floating-point spellings such as NaN and Infinity are not valid numbers.
hints: Separate the mantissa rules from the stricter exponent rules.
Scan once while tracking whether a digit, dot, and exponent marker have appeared.
Allow a sign only at the beginning or immediately after e/E. At e/E require a mantissa digit and reset the digit flag so exponent digits become mandatory.
After an exponent, reject dots and another exponent. Accept only if the current digit flag is true at the end.
editorial: Use state flags to validate syntax without converting the number or risking overflow. A dot is legal at most once and only before the exponent. The exponent marker requires an existing digit and clears that flag to enforce a nonempty exponent. A sign is permitted only at the beginning or just after the exponent marker. The independent oracle uses an anchored regular-expression grammar; regression tests also enumerate short strings against a separate grammar decomposition. Numeric magnitude is irrelevant: an exponent may be too large for machine floats while its spelling is valid.

tests.explanation: A single digit is an integer, and no exponent is required.
The mantissa 99 is valid, but an exponent cannot contain a decimal point, so this string is invalid.
